metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.note: 6 numbered boxes in the carbon cycle flow diagram; 3 marks total at 0.5 marks per correct box. Carbon cycle is a core CSEC Biology topic across all recent papers.

question.name: CSEC Bio Jan 2024 Q3a(i) — Carbon Cycle Diagram Completion
question.text:
Figure 3 shows the carbon cycle as a flow diagram with six numbered boxes (I–VI) to complete. The diagram shows:

  • Box I (top) → arrows point DOWN to a tree and a bush
  • Arrow from bush → Box II → Box I (upward cycle)
  • Arrow from tree and cow → Box IV → Box I
  • Arrow from cow (Death) → Box V
  • Box V → factory (combustion) → Box I
  • Box V → Box III → Box I
  • Box VI (very bottom, near Death and decomposition)

Insert the correct name of the process or substance for each numbered space.
question.general_feedback:
Complete carbon cycle:
Box I = Carbon dioxide (CO₂) — the atmospheric carbon reservoir
Box II = Photosynthesis — plants absorb CO₂ and fix it into organic compounds
Box III = Decomposition — decomposers break down dead matter, releasing CO₂
Box IV = Respiration — living organisms release CO₂ through cellular respiration
Box V = Dead organisms — remains of dead plants and animals
Box VI = Fossil fuels — ancient organic matter stored underground; released by combustion

Key concept: Photosynthesis removes CO₂ from the atmosphere; respiration, decomposition, and combustion all return CO₂ to the atmosphere. This balance is being disrupted by burning fossil fuels.

ddwtos.cloze_html:
Box I (top — the atmospheric carbon store): [[1]]

Box II (process: plants → atmosphere): [[2]]

Box III (process: dead organisms → atmosphere): [[3]]

groups.label: Box I — the atmospheric carbon store
groups.diagnostic_hint: Box I is carbon dioxide (CO₂) — the form of carbon found in the atmosphere. All other carbon cycle processes either remove CO₂ from or return CO₂ to this atmospheric reservoir. Oxygen (O₂) and nitrogen (N₂) are also in the atmosphere but are not the carbon store.

groups.label: Box II — process by which plants absorb CO₂ from the atmosphere
groups.diagnostic_hint: Box II is photosynthesis — the process by which green plants absorb CO₂ from the air and convert it into glucose using sunlight energy. This is the main process that REMOVES carbon from the atmosphere. Respiration does the opposite — it returns CO₂ to the atmosphere.

groups.label: Box III — process by which dead organic matter releases CO₂
groups.diagnostic_hint: Box III is decomposition — the breakdown of dead organisms by decomposers (bacteria and fungi), releasing CO₂ back into the atmosphere. Don't confuse with combustion (burning) — combustion applies to fossil fuels or wood burned by humans, not biological decomposition of recent dead matter.

groups.label: Box IV — process by which living organisms release CO₂
groups.diagnostic_hint: Box IV is respiration (cellular respiration) — the process by which ALL living organisms (plants, animals, fungi) break down glucose to release energy, releasing CO₂ as a by-product. Both the cow and the tree undergo respiration. Transpiration is the evaporation of water from leaves — not a carbon cycle process.

groups.label: Box V — substance formed when organisms die (before decomposition/fossilisation)
groups.diagnostic_hint: Box V is dead organisms — the remains of recently dead plants and animals. This is the intermediate store between living organisms and either decomposition (short timescale) or fossilisation into fossil fuels (geological timescale). 'Fossil fuels' is wrong here — fossil fuels are ancient compressed dead organisms, not the fresh remains.

groups.label: Box VI — ancient carbon substance burned in factory (combustion)
groups.diagnostic_hint: Box VI is fossil fuels (coal, oil, natural gas) — formed over millions of years from compressed dead organisms. When burned (combustion) in factories and engines, they release CO₂ back into the atmosphere. This distinguishes them from 'dead organisms' (Box V), which are recent remains undergoing decomposition.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 10 tokens for 6 slots: 6 correct + 4 distractors. Key distractor pairs: Decomposition vs Combustion (both release CO₂ from non-living matter, but different agents); Photosynthesis vs Respiration (opposite processes, high-value distractor); Dead organisms vs Fossil fuels (temporal distinction — recent vs ancient).
